tile-installation/palmetto.title: Tile Installation in Palmetto, FL | Kitchens & Baths
tile-installation/palmetto.description: Tile installers serving Palmetto, FL bathrooms, kitchens and showers, from Old Palmetto terrazzo repairs to Riviera Dunes waterfront remodels. 2026 pricing.
tile-installation/palmetto.lede: Tile installation in Palmetto splits between historic-district kitchens and baths downtown and full wet-area remodels in Riviera Dunes and Snead Island waterfront homes.
tile-installation/palmetto.capsule: Tile installation in Palmetto splits between two very different jobs: kitchen and bath work in Old Palmetto's 1900s-1960s bungalows, where cracked original tile or brittle terrazzo often needs a full grind-and-reseal, and wet-area and shower tile in Riviera Dunes condos and Snead Island custom homes. Typical 2026 installed ranges run $6 to $22 per sq ft, with a Kerdi shower running $1,800 to $3,800.
tile-installation/palmetto.body_html:
Kitchens and baths carry most of the tile installation work we do in Palmetto's historic core. Old Palmetto and the blocks around the Palmetto Historic District are largely 1900s-1960s bungalows and block homes, and a fair number of these turn up cracked original ceramic tile or thin, brittle terrazzo under later flooring that needs a full grind-and-reseal rather than a simple polish before anything new goes down. Because the flooring budget on these jobs is usually competing with other renovation trades, whole-house tile is rare here; owners tile the wet areas and put vinyl plank or another product everywhere else.

Riviera Dunes and Snead Island are where we do our largest tile jobs in Palmetto, and the driver there is water exposure rather than budget. Marina-front condos and custom homes on the river commonly need a curbless or linear-drain shower system, and porcelain plank in a wood-look finish shows up more than natural stone, since it holds up to the higher ambient humidity near the Manatee River without the sealing upkeep stone requires. A 2,200 sq ft Riviera Dunes townhome redoing two bathrooms and a kitchen backsplash would typically pair large-format 24″+ porcelain on the floors with a Kerdi shower system in the primary bath.

Flood zone matters here too, since the same AE designations that run along the river downtown extend to Snead Island and the blocks near Regatta Pointe Marina, and while tile itself tolerates water exposure fine, the plywood or particleboard substrate under an older floor sometimes doesn't, so we check subfloor condition before quoting large-format tile in any home built before the 2000s in these pockets. Inland at Trevesta and Artisan Lakes, newer construction means a flatter, more consistent slab, and large-format tile goes down with less prep work than it would over an older, settled downtown foundation.

Whatever the neighborhood, tile itself doesn't trigger a building permit in most Florida jurisdictions, Palmetto included, but a curbless shower or any work touching the wet-area membrane goes through the City of Palmetto Building Department for in-city addresses.
tile-installation/palmetto.cost_html:
A 2,200 sq ft Riviera Dunes townhome tiling two bathroom floors plus a kitchen backsplash: roughly 400 sq ft of large-format 24″+ porcelain at $9-$15 per sq ft ($3,600-$6,000), a Kerdi shower system at $1,800-$3,800, and a 30 sq ft backsplash at $22-$45 per sq ft ($660-$1,350), for a project total of about $6,060-$11,150.

An Old Palmetto kitchen and bath re-tile in standard 12-18″ porcelain runs $6-$10 per sq ft, so 250 sq ft comes to $1,500-$2,500 before any grind-and-reseal work on the original slab, which adds separately. Full breakdowns are in our tile installation cost guide.

faqs.q: Do downtown Palmetto homes often have original terrazzo or ceramic tile underneath?
faqs.a: Some do. Houses in the historic district built before the 1960s sometimes have original tile or thin terrazzo under later flooring, and it usually needs a full grind-and-reseal rather than a quick polish once it's uncovered.

faqs.q: What shower system do you recommend for a Riviera Dunes or Snead Island bathroom?
faqs.a: A Kerdi or curbless linear-drain system, given how much waterfront work we do in both areas. The higher ambient humidity near the Manatee River is also why we lean toward porcelain over natural stone on those jobs.

faqs.q: Does tile work in a Palmetto AE flood zone need special permitting?
faqs.a: Tile itself is exempt from a permit in most Florida jurisdictions, Palmetto included, but a curbless shower or anything touching the wet-area membrane goes through the City of Palmetto Building Department for addresses inside city limits.
